func (c *Config) validate() error {
	if c.Server.Protocol == HTTPS {
		if c.Server.CertFile == "" {
			return errors.New("cert_file cannot be empty when using HTTPS")
		}

		if c.Server.CertKey == "" {
			return errors.New("cert_key cannot be empty when using HTTPS")
		}

		if _, err := os.Stat(c.Server.CertFile); os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return fmt.Errorf("cannot find TLS cert_file at %q", c.Server.CertFile)
		}

		if _, err := os.Stat(c.Server.CertKey); os.IsNotExist(err) {
			return fmt.Errorf("cannot find TLS cert_key at %q", c.Server.CertKey)
		}
	}

	return nil
}

item.text: The loader starts from `Default()` and applies only keys Viper reports as present, so the pool fields can follow that pattern. One requirement says an omitted update flag must be `false`, while another requires omitted keys to preserve `Default()`. I’ll make the default update flag `false`, then load explicit values when present; that satisfies both behaviors and keeps the default fixtures equal to `Default()`.

The loader now reads all three pool settings and `meta.check_for_updates`; omitted update checks default to `false`. I updated the existing advanced config fixture to include pool values and an explicit `true`, while the existing defaults cases continue to compare against `Default()`. The config package tests pass; I’m reviewing the final diff now.
